The test image shows a close-up of a soybean stem: bleached/gray-white coloration with dark speckling (black dots/pycnidia) on the stem surface. Stem appears dead and dry. This pattern suggests Phomopsis or Charcoal Rot as top candidates.

Now I'll view references one at a time, starting with my top candidates and then covering all 16 classes.
Phomopsis_14 shows a pod/seed, not matching the stem pattern. Let me check Charcoal Rot.
Charcoal_Rot_116 shows tiny black sclerotia on pale/bleached tissue — very similar pattern to the test image! This is a strong match. Now checking Anthracnose.
Anthracnose shows darker brown stem lesions, not the bleached gray with speckling. Continuing with other classes.
White_Mold_133 shows bleached stem with large dark sclerotia — somewhat similar but those are bigger/distinct. Continuing to cover more classes.
Brown_Stem_Rot shows internal brown pith rot — not matching. One more class needed.

Now I have 16 reference views. Let me summarize my analysis:

**Test image features:**
- Close-up of a single soybean stem
- Bleached/gray-white coloration
- Fine dark speckling (tiny black dots) uniformly distributed across the stem surface
- Hairy soybean stem surface visible
- Dry/dead tissue, background of debris

**Comparison results:**
- **Charcoal_Rot_116**: Strong match — shows tiny black microsclerotia (salt-and-pepper pattern) on pale bleached stem tissue, nearly identical pattern
- **White_Mold_133**: Bleached stem but with large, distinct oblong black sclerotia — too coarse vs. the fine speckling in the test image
- **Phomopsis**: All 3 references showed pods/seeds, not the stem speckling pattern
- **Anthracnose, Brown_Stem_Rot, Septoria, Cercospora, Frogeye, Bacterial_Blight, SDS, Phytophthora, Soybean_rust**: None show the bleached stem + fine dark speckling pattern

The gray-white bleached stem covered in uniformly fine dark microsclerotia is the hallmark of Charcoal Rot (*Macrophomina phaseolina*). The Charcoal_Rot_116 reference image is the closest visual match.
